$comment: Pinned model cards of the vision demos. The model files are never committed: scripts/vision-models.mjs downloads them into demos/vision-assets/models/ (git-ignored) and verifies size and SHA-256. `spec` is a ModelSpec (contracts/vision/README.md) WITHOUT labels: `labels` names the labels file (one label per line); load it, set it as spec.labels and call parseModelSpec. `io.input` is the input tensor name and `io.outputs` maps each tensor name the @ilabs/vision decoders read (scores for a classifier; boxes, classes, scores, count for the `ssd` format) to the model's output tensor name; for TFLite `io.outputIndex` gives the output tensor index of the same names.

models.name: MobileNetV2 1.0 (ImageNet-1k), ONNX

license.note: The model page ends with 'License: Apache 2.0'; the repository LICENSE is Apache-2.0 too. The URL is pinned to the commit c5cae0f (the file is stored with Git LFS; the SHA-256 equals the LFS object id of that commit).

models.notes: Input [1,3,224,224] float32, values (byte / 255 - mean) / std. The model page asks for resize to 256 then centre crop 224; the centerCrop mode resizes the short side straight to 224, a slightly tighter crop. Output [1,1000] logits. Checked by running the model (onnxruntime-node).

models.name: SSD-MobileNet v1 (COCO), ONNX

license.note: The model page ends with 'MIT License' (the onnx/models repository itself is Apache-2.0; the original TensorFlow Object Detection API model is Apache-2.0). Both are Apache-2.0 compatible. Same commit pin and LFS note as the classifier.

models.notes: Input [1,H,W,3] uint8 (any size; 300x300 is the training size and is used here). Outputs: detection_boxes [1,100,4] as [ymin,xmin,ymax,xmax] normalized to 0..1, detection_classes [1,100] float class ids, detection_scores [1,100], num_detections [1]. The class ids are the COCO category ids 1..90 (person = 1; ids 12, 26, 29, 30, 45, 66, 68, 69, 71 and 83 are unused): coco-90.txt holds one line per id starting at id 1, hence labelOffset 1. The model applies its own non-maximum suppression, so the ssd decoder default (nms false) is right. Checked by running the model (onnxruntime-node).

models.name: EfficientNet-Lite0 (ImageNet-1k), TFLite

license.note: The model card of the litert-community repository declares apache-2.0 and the TFLite metadata embedded in the file states 'Apache License. Version 2.0' (author MediaPipe). The URL is Google's versioned MediaPipe model bucket path (float32/1).

models.notes: Input [1,224,224,3] float32, values (byte - 127) / 128 (the normalization of the embedded metadata). Output [1,1000] probabilities (the graph ends in a softmax). The labels are the same 1000 ImageNet-1k names, in the same order, as the model's own labels_without_background.txt (checked byte for byte). Read from the file's tensors and metadata; not run in this repository (no TFLite runtime was available on the capture machine).

models.name: SSD-MobileNet v1 (COCO, quantized), TFLite

license.note: The TFLite metadata embedded in the file states 'Apache License. Version 2.0' (author TensorFlow); the file is the model of the TensorFlow Lite Task Library object detection example.

models.notes: Input [1,300,300,3] uint8 (raw bytes). Outputs (up to 10 detections): boxes [1,10,4] as [ymin,xmin,ymax,xmax] normalized, classes [1,10] float, scores [1,10], count [1]. Following the TensorFlow Lite object detection example, the classes are 0-based indices into the 90 lines of coco-90.txt (person = 0): labelOffset 0, unlike the ONNX build whose ids are the COCO category ids (labelOffset 1). Input and output tensors were read from the file; the class convention comes from the TFLite example and was not run in this repository (no TFLite runtime was available on the capture machine): confirm it on a device.
